title: Protocol for preparing sensor molecules and analyzing heterotypic endomembrane fusion in insulin-responsive cells using live-cell imaging
protocol: Dilute Cellmatrix Type IV collagen to 10× with 1 mM HCl.
Cover the glass surface of the glass-bottom dishes with 150 μL of diluted Cellmatrix Type IV collagen solution.
Keep the glass-bottom dishes for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Remove excess fluid from the coated surface and allow them to dry for 16–20 h at 4°C.
Rinse with PBS twice before introducing cells and medium.
Seed 2×10^5 undifferentiated 3T3L1 fibroblasts in growth medium into a 150-mm dish (day 0).
Incubate the cells at 37°C at 8% CO2 for 8 days with medium change at day 4.
At day 8, switch to differentiation medium and incubate the cells at 37°C at 8% CO2 for 4 days.
Switch to insulin medium and incubate the cells at 37°C with 8% CO2 for at least 2 days.
Confirm accumulation of lipid droplets in cells using brightfield observation.
Harvest differentiated adipocytes.
Dilute cell suspension to 4× concentration.
Seed 200 μL of cell suspension onto collagen IV-coated glass bottom dishes.
Incubate seeded cells at 37°C with 8% CO2 for 1 day.
Dissolve each 10–25 μg myc-GLUT4-mCherry and TfR plasmid DNAs in 100 μL of electroporation buffer.
Remove culture medium from the dishes.
Add plasmid solution to the cells.
Apply poration pulse at 200 V for 10 ms, followed by five driving pulses at -30 V for 10 ms with intervals of 50 ms between each pulse.
Add 2 mL of feed medium to the electroporated cells.
Incubate cells in feed medium for 1–2 days.
Seed 8×10^4 3T3L1 fibroblasts in growth medium into a 35-mm glass bottom dish.
Incubate seeded fibroblasts at 37°C with 8% CO2 for 1 day.
Dilute 4.5 μL of Lipofectamine 3000 reagent in 125 μL of Opti-MEM medium.
Mix the diluted Lipofectamine 3000 reagent well.
Dilute 1 μg each of myc-GLUT4-mCherry, HA-sortilin, and HaloTag-AS160 plasmid DNAs in 125 μL of Opti-MEM medium.
Add 6 μL of P3000 reagent to the diluted DNA mixture.
Mix the DNA-P3000 solution well.
Add the diluted DNA-P3000 mixture to the diluted Lipofectamine 3000 reagent.
Incubate the combined mixture for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Add the solution dropwise to the cells.
Incubate the cells at 37°C in an atmosphere of 8% CO2 for 4 h.
Change the medium after the incubation period.
Incubate the cells for an additional day.
Culture hybridoma cells in vessels that can continuously stir cell suspensions.
Collect conditioned medium from the culture and spin down at 1,000×g for 3 minutes.
Keep supernatant after spinning down the conditioned medium.
Filter the supernatant to remove debris.
Pour Protein G Sepharose slurry into a column in one continuous motion.
Fill the remainder of the column with PBS and equilibrate the slurry with at least twice the volume of column bed material in PBS.
Apply collected conditioned medium at a flow rate of approximately 2 mL/min.
Wash the column with at least ten times the volume of column bed material in PBS after applying all conditioned medium.
Prepare six 1.5 mL tubes containing 50 μL of 1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.5).
Add 0.2 M glycine buffer (pH 2.5) into the column and collect eluates (1 mL in each 1.5 mL tube).
Measure absorbance at 280 nm to identify fractions containing antibodies.
Exchange buffer with PBS-EDTA by ultrafiltration using an Amicon Ultra-4 100k MWCO filter.
Critical: Presence of EDTA is critical for stabilizing half-antibodies since EDTA prevents oxidation of sulfhydryl groups.
Determine antibody concentration.
Dilute or concentrate antibodies to prepare a 10 mg/mL solution in PBS-EDTA.
Exchange buffer in streptavidin stock solution for sodium bicarbonate buffer through ultrafiltration using Amicon Ultra-4 10k MWCO.
Determine streptavidin concentration using absorption at 280 nm with an extinction coefficient of 3.2 cm\(^{-1}\).
Dilute or concentrate this streptavidin to a 10 mg/mL solution in sodium bicarbonate buffer.
Add 200 μL of streptavidin into a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 3 μL of BODIPY FL-NHS to the contents of the tube.
Mix the contents at 800 rpm for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Exchange buffer for PBS through ultrafiltration using Amicon Ultra-4 10k MWCO.
Determine protein concentration using absorption at 280 nm and 504 nm.
Dissolve sulfo-SMCC in Milli-Q water to a concentration of 5 mg/mL.
Immediately after dissolving, add 10-fold molar amount of sulfo-SMCC to BODIPY-labeled streptavidin.
Rock gently for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Exchange buffer for PBS-EDTA through ultrafiltration using Amicon Ultra-4 10k MWCO.
Dissolve 6 mg of 2-mercaptoethylamine in 100 μL of PBS-EDTA.
Add 1 μL of the 2-mercaptoethylamine solution to each 10 μL volume of 10 mg/mL antibodies.
Rock gently for 1.5 h at 37°C.
Exchange buffer for PBS-EDTA through ultrafiltration using Amicon Ultra-4 10k MWCO.
Combine anti-myc half-antibodies and maleimide-activated SA/BODIPY at a 1:1.2 molar ratio.
Rock gently for 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Exchange buffer for PBS through ultrafiltration using Amicon Ultra-4 10k MWCO.
Prepare 100 nM of anti-myc-SA/BODIPY in PBS.
Prepare 1 μM of Tf-biotin in PBS.
Mix anti-myc-SA/BODIPY and Tf-biotin to prepare mixtures with ratios from 1:0 to 1:32.
Rock the mixture gently for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Measure fluorescence intensity using a spectrofluorometer (excitation at 488 nm, emission at 515 nm).
Incubate the cells with serum-free medium at 37°C in an 8% CO2 environment for 1 hour.
Treat the cells with 4 μg/mL anti-myc-SA/BODIPY and 1 nM insulin for 1 hour.
Rinse the cells three times with serum-free medium.
Incubate the cells for at least 3 hours, exchanging the medium every hour.
Rinse the cells twice with imaging buffer.
Incubate the cells in 1 mL of imaging buffer for 10 minutes.
Place the cells under a confocal microscope to search for proper localization of myc-GLUT4-mCherry around perinuclear regions.
Add 10 mL of Imaging buffer containing 5 μg/mL Tf-biotin by perifusion and incubate for 5 minutes.
Wash the cells thoroughly with 30 mL of Imaging buffer by perifusion.
Incubate for 8 min.
Start image acquisition.
Add 10 mL of Imaging buffer containing 100 nM insulin 2 min after initiation of image acquisition.
Continue image acquisition for further 10 min.
Save acquired images as a lif (Leica image format) or tiff files.
Open the acquired BODIPY and mCherry images (e.g., a1/b1 and a2/b2 images in Figures 5A and 5B, respectively) with Fiji ImageJ.
Set “Divide by zero value” in Fiji (Edit > Options > Misc…) to 0.

Create a new image as a 32-bit floating-point data by dividing each BODIPY frame image by each corresponding mCherry frame image with Image Calculator of Fiji and save it as a “ratio image” (e.g., a3/b3 images in Figures 5A and 5B).
Set ROI for analysis by extracting cell contours using the mCherry image.
Apply Gaussian Blur filter to each mCherry frame image to smooth the contour.
Binarize the images.
Run “Analyze Particles” of Fiji over all frames with turning on “Add to Manager” to add the measured particles to the “ROI Manager”.
Measure ratio value within cellular regions (R) and area above threshold (S) for each frame using ROI obtained in previous steps.
Calculate mean R and S values for the frames imaged during the 2-min period before insulin stimulation (defined as R0 and S0, respectively).
Calculate normalized changes in R from R0, i.e., (R–R0)/R0 (defined as ΔRnormalized).
Calculate changes in S from S0, i.e., S–S0 (defined as ΔS).
Calculate the index of insulin-responsive heterotypic fusion ΔF as the product obtained by multiplying ΔRnormalized and ΔS.
